newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan hopes for bumper crop despite pest attack.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan hopes for bumper crop despite pest attack.

text.p: Pakistan expects a bumper cotton crop of over 10 million 375-lb bales in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), despite a recent flare-up of pests in the central Punjab province, officials and dealers said on Thursday.
"There has been some damage but the situation is not alarming at the moment," Zahoor Ahmed, director of the state-run Cotton Research Institute, told Reuters in a telephone interview from Multan.
He said assessments and surveys carried out by his institute and other government departments showed "limited damage" to the crop, in spite of an unusually high infestation of White Fly.
The infestation was mostly concentrated in the central Punjab province, the major cotton producing area.
"The White Fly infestation was unusually high but the impact of Leaf Curl Virus (LCV) was normal, and in our assessment the overall damage has not been of an alarming proportion," Ahmed noted.

Pakistan achieved a yield of 9.95 million bales in the 1995/96 financial year, against 7.7 million in 1994/95 when the crop was poor for the third year in a row. Officials blamed LCV attacks and flash floods for the poor levels of production in those years.

"The (state-run) Crop Estimation Committee had a meeting in Karachi a few days back where officials, farmers and ginners expressed their satisfaction over the pace of arrivals and the health of the crop," Ahmed said.
He added that the committee will meet again by mid-October when the picking season, which started in September, will be at its peak.
Cotton dealers in Karachi, however, were divided over the the health and production estimates of the current crop.
"We were expecting a crop of 11 million bales. Even if the pests have eaten up 500,000 bales, which is an estimate of the higher side, we will still get 10.5 million bales," dealer Nasim Usman said.
He blamed people with vested interests for spreading rumours regarding the extent of crop damage, as they were benefitting from the soaring prices.
Usman noted that the NIAB-78 variety jumped 50 rupees ($1.34) to close at 2,200 rupees on Wednesday as spinners fearing a lower crop output covered their future requirements.

But dealer Mustafa Hussain said the White Fly damage could be well above 15 percent of the total crop planted in the central Punjab province, slashing the final production figure to 9.5 million bales.

Maqbool Sadiq, Chairman of the Karachi Cotton Association, said the damage has been "susbstantial" but added that his association stood by the final production figure of 10 million bales calculated by the Crop Estimation Committee.
"We are taking the situation with a note of caution but it would be too early to say if the pest attack will bring the production below the target of 10 million bales," Sadiq said.
